$comment: Invariant ids owned by the P2 round-3 task `p2r3/provenance-docs`. The list is EMPTY and that is the whole truth about this lane: it writes prose and one rubric, and it writes no test. Prose cannot falsify an invariant. The brief named INV-PACK-17 as the id this lane serves — the credits surface S152 and its two entry points — and serving an id is not owning it: the pack half is already gated by validator F3 and by test_g9_package.py::test_INV_PACK_17_fails_the_stage_and_writes_nothing, and the screen half is P4's, because the screen does not exist. A test in this lane could only assert that a markdown file contains a string, and naming that after an invariant about attribution reachability is exactly the 'owning test that proves nothing' the plan's rule 4 is written against. So: no id claimed, and the reason is written here instead of padded into the list.

serves.INV-PACK-17: Every sentence, voice and derived list whose licence requires attribution is reachable from the rendered credits surface (S152), itself reachable from the report sheet (S045) and About (S137). This lane wrote down the surface: docs/pack-provenance.md now carries S152 in its surface table with all ten copy slots from the product map's Surface 16 — nine backticked strings plus the per-row `sentence text` the corpus writes unbackticked — its five states, both entry-point strings, and the no-network property. That is build material for P4, not coverage. THE ID IS ALREADY OWNED AND MUST NOT BE RE-CLAIMED: docs/owned/p2-g9.json on origin/main reads "owned": ["INV-PACK-17", "INV-PACK-41"], and scripts/coverage-map.ts errors when two ownership files claim the same id — so a later lane that read this note as an invitation would turn CI red. What is genuinely unowned is the `E` half: p2-g9.json's own propertyTests entry says "the `E` half is P4's, when S152 exists to walk", and P4 adds that as an e2e test under the id p2-g9 already owns rather than as a second claim.

deliverables.what: Eight release prerequisites, with the paid native-speaker review of every shipped language first: 300 items, a wrong-item rate at or below 2%, $300-800 per language times four shipped languages. Then the things a release blocks on that this run cannot do: signing key custody exercised on a real manifest (the pack key exists from P0 and has never signed anything, because no pack has ever been built), the ten D-kind invariant ids plus the four unlabelled manual items, EAS Starter at $19/month, and the Apple/Play identities that do not exist at all. Then the three that are writing or work rather than money: the suite and e2e, the README honesty block, and the mutation score marked explicitly non-gating.
deliverables.why: Founder ruling B3 made the paid review a release prerequisite and named this file as where it is listed. Writing it at P2 rather than P8 is the point: four of the eight cost money or need a person, so they have lead times, and a lead time discovered at P8 is a blocker discovered too late.

deliverables.what: A sixth scored dimension, `accent_consistency`, named, defined and scoreable: three ordered questions (is it one accent / is it the variety the course teaches / is it the same cast row to row), the two blended roles with their weights and the specific question content/es/cast.yaml promises the reviewer gets asked, the verdict mapping (accent-only failure is `awkward` with a note prefixed `accent:`, never folded into the wrong-item rate), and the reporting rule. Also: the B3 ruling quoted where 'who is scoring' is explained, the locale sentence corrected from `es-ES` to `language: es` + `accent_claim: unverified`, and the row-format example left at FIVE dimensions on purpose: `accent_consistency` is not in REVIEW_DIMENSIONS on this branch or on any sibling p2r3 branch, and a canonical example carrying the key would be the one action the file twice forbids — a reviewer copying it would make read_scores raise and destroy the rate for the whole sheet. The sixth-key form is shown separately under a heading that says not to use it yet, with the one-line command that checks the constant.
deliverables.why: B6 demoted the accent claim to something nothing in the toolchain can falsify. The 300-item sample is the last place a Latin-American-sounding peninsular course can be caught, so the clause is load-bearing rather than a nicety, and it has to be a scored column and not a paragraph of advice.

measuredHere.claim: INV-PACK-18 is owned and green, so docs/RELEASE.md §2 must not say the invariant has no owning test — only that the END-TO-END PATH is unexercised.
measuredHere.how: A previous attempt of this lane asserted in RELEASE.md that 'INV-PACK-18 ... has no owning test and never has'. That was false and it was false in the one document whose purpose is honest accounting. Measured: `grep -c "it('\[INV-PACK-18\]" packages/core/src/packs/*.test.ts` gives 9 in install.test.ts, 3 in state.test.ts, 1 in falsifiers.test.ts = 13 owning tests; install.test.ts:82 opens describe('INV-PACK-18 verify before install'); :83 asserts result.steps equals ['parse-manifest','verify-signature','verify-payload-digest','install'] AND indexOf('verify-signature') < indexOf('install'), so the ordering guard is load-bearing rather than name-only; :96 asserts a wrong key yields state 'unverified' with installed false and never 'corrupt'. The id is owned at docs/owned/packs.json (P1 task p1-packs-data-security), and `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/coverage-map.ts` EXITS 0 reporting 'OK INV-PACK-18 <- 23 test(s)', which is impossible for an unowned id. RELEASE.md now splits the three claims that were conflated: the RULE is owned and green, the SIGNATURE has never been produced (no pack exists), and the PATH — a device refusing a foreign-signed pack — has never run. Only the last two are release prerequisites.

crossLaneContracts.producedBy: the validator/sample lane (p2r3/validators-ci-loader and its successors)
crossLaneContracts.consumedBy: content/es/review/RUBRIC.md, which names the dimension a reviewer scores
crossLaneContracts.assertion: the tuple contains the exact string `accent_consistency`
crossLaneContracts.why: THIS IS THE ONE CONTRACT IN THIS LANE THAT CAN BREAK SOMETHING. sample.py::read_scores raises ScoreError on any `dimensions` key outside REVIEW_DIMENSIONS and the caller turns that into exit 4 — so a rubric and a constant that disagree do not produce a slightly wrong rate, they produce NO rate for the whole file, including the five text dimensions that were scored correctly. The rubric could not add the key itself: config/sample.py is not in this lane's file list, and the brief said to coordinate on the name rather than invent one. No sibling lane was reachable to coordinate with (ListAgents showed no peer implementer for this round), so the name was chosen and written down here with its failure mode instead of guessed at silently.
crossLaneContracts.whyThisSpelling: `accent` was rejected deliberately. In a Spanish rubric `accent` reads first as the orthographic diacritic — the codebase is full of that sense already (INV-PACK-10's own test is named `a_candidate_one_accent_from_correct_is_discarded_not_corrected`) — so a dimension called `accent` in a file about Spanish text would be misread by the first reviewer who met it. `accent_consistency` matches the ruling's own wording ('the reviewer rubric checks accent consistency') and the two-word snake form is already precedented by `answer_set`.
crossLaneContracts.ifTheSpellingDiffers: Whoever lands the constant wins; the rubric moves to match, and it is a two-line edit in one table plus one JSON example. RUBRIC.md points at the constant as the authority in the sentence that introduces the table, so the direction of the fix is already written down. Until the constant carries any spelling at all, RUBRIC.md §'If the constant does not carry it yet' tells a scorer to put the finding in `note` prefixed `accent:` and not in `dimensions`, so a sheet scored in the gap still produces a rate.

crossLaneContracts.assertion: both files carry `PROVISIONAL (unreviewed by a paid native speaker)` byte-identically; pack-provenance.md contains the substrings `two places that exist today`, `S001` and `does not exist yet`, and does NOT contain `appears in exactly four places`
crossLaneContracts.why: Those two tests open these documents and read them. Every edit in this lane was made around them: the note string was never retyped (it is quoted, never paraphrased, and the surrounding prose changed while the block did not), the carrier table kept its four rows and its wording, and the manifest row's 'does not exist yet' was sharpened with a paragraph rather than replaced. The tests live in the sample lane's file, so a documentation lane that reworded them would have broken a test it could not fix.

crossLaneContracts.producedBy: the founder, per ruling B5 — the corpus is research and no phase agent may rewrite it
crossLaneContracts.consumedBy: docs/pack-provenance.md and tools/coursekit/README.md, which quote its copy slots so a P4 implementer does not have to read the corpus
crossLaneContracts.assertion: all TEN copy slots are quoted verbatim: the nine backticked strings — `Credits`, `Content credits`, `Credits for this sentence`, `Source: {{source}}`, `Licence: {{licence}}`, `By {{owner}}`, `Frequency ordering derived from FrequencyWords (hermitdave), CC BY-SA 4.0`, `Voices: Kokoro (Apache-2.0)`, `This pack is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0` — plus the per-row slot the corpus writes without backticks as "per row: sentence text".
crossLaneContracts.why: The map is the P3/P4 build contract and it lives outside the repository, so nothing in CI can hold a repo doc against it. A copy slot that drifted here would be a screen built wrong with a document saying it was right. Whoever builds S152 should diff these two tables against the corpus row rather than trusting either. The sentence-text slot is the one a quoter loses, because it is the only slot Surface 16 does not backtick: an earlier draft of both tables quoted nine strings and called it the whole contract, which would have built a credits list of sources and owners with no sentence beside them, and made the map's 'searchable by sentence text' unimplementable. Both tables now carry it and say why it is easy to drop.

crossLaneContracts.consumedBy: S137 About and S001's pack card, and the claim in docs/pack-provenance.md about which carriers hold the honesty note

crossLaneContracts.why: Today `"defectRate": inputs.defect_rate` is a bare value and `review` is not a manifest field, so the doc says the manifest carrier does not exist yet — and test_the_docs_do_not_claim_the_note_already_appears_where_it_cannot enforces that it keeps saying so. The day G9 adds the note, that test's expectations and this paragraph both need changing, in the same commit.

heldWithoutAnInvariantId: docs/RELEASE.md has no test and cannot have one: every row is a purchase, a person or a signature. The closest thing to a gate is that the paid-review row and the PROVISIONAL string are the same fact from two directions, and the string is already tested.

The accent-consistency dimension is defined and NOT YET SCOREABLE, and the rubric says so at the point of use rather than letting the first reviewer discover it. SampleItem carries ten fields and none of them is a clip or a voice role, so there is nothing to listen to; written up as B18 with the two fields it needs, the reviewer-package problem (build/ is gitignored and es-build-<sha> retains for 7 days, which is the failure mode that killed pack-bake.yml), and the SAMPLE_STRATA question that rides along — the draw does not stratify over voice role, so a 300-row sheet could answer the blend question with four Rosa rows.

No status in docs/P2-BLOCKERS.md was moved to RESOLVED on the strength of a ruling. DECIDED and BUILT are separate words in that table for exactly that reason, and five rulings are recorded as decided-and-not-built: B6 (three of five parts), B9 (all three parts), B14, B16 (the reader), B17. A table that had read them as resolved would have turned eight answered questions into eight invisible pieces of outstanding work.

The B3 gate observation is the one finding in this lane that is a code hazard rather than a document: gate_passed() is reviewer-kind-blind, so a release build can call it, get true off an agent-scored sheet, and be correct by the code and wrong by the ruling. Two honest options are written into B3 (a `require_paid` parameter, or leaving the release checklist as the only gate); sample.py is not in this lane, so it is filed rather than fixed.
